cues: Change the temperature, and the product changes.
At one seventy degrees each ethanol molecule loses its own water: ethene.
At one forty degrees, with excess alcohol, two molecules share one water, giving ethoxyethane, diethyl ether.
Where two alkenes are possible, Saytzeff's rule applies again: butan two ol gives mainly but two ene.
